rubrics.criterion: Both table-to-page conversion paths on the write path (plain-encoding and dictionary-encoding) produce each page's statistics (maximum, minimum, null count) inside one grouped carrier returned alongside the pages, so neither path still hands its caller three parallel member collections.
rubrics.rationale: The two slicing functions in the layout package are the production origin of the per-page statistics record for every column written; leaving either one emitting separated members keeps the record ungrouped at its source.

rubrics.criterion: Every page-header serialization form on the write path (the standard data-page header, the dictionary-encoded data-page header, and the v2-header compatibility form) fills its header Statistics from one grouped statistics carrier rather than from members received as separate individual values.
rubrics.rationale: All three serialization helpers in the layout package were widened to accept the record's members separately, including the v2 form that ordinary runs do not exercise, so a complete resolution must reach all of them, not just the default path.

rubrics.criterion: Both pages-to-chunk aggregation functions consume each page's statistics through the grouped carrier when folding per-page maxima, minima, and null counts into chunk metadata, and a dictionary page still contributes no statistics to its column chunk.
rubrics.rationale: The chunk-level fold is where per-page statistics become the column metadata readers rely on, and the dictionary-chunk function is a separate aggregation site whose leading dictionary-page position has always been excluded.

rubrics.criterion: Between object flush and row-group flush the writer holds every column's buffered page statistics inside one grouping that stays attached to the buffered pages through the parallel-flush merge and row-group assembly, instead of three buffered member collections kept index-aligned with the page buffer by hand.
rubrics.rationale: The writer is the participant that must retain the record across the parallel worker merge, the merge order, the row-group-time chunk call, and the reset after each row group; this is where mispairing between a page and its statistics can silently corrupt chunk metadata and column indexes.

rubrics.criterion: Construction paths that assemble the writer state directly instead of going through the shared constructor (the arrow-schema writer entry point) set up, or are excused from needing, every piece of statistics-buffering state the refactored design requires, so the second entry point runs against fully initialized state.
rubrics.rationale: This adapter builds the base writer state by hand, so any change to what the writer must allocate for statistics buffering obligates the same change there; an entry point left stale is invisible to the layout packages and panics or loses statistics only when it is used.

rubrics.criterion: The grouped statistics carrier crosses the layout-to-writer interface as the same representation on both sides, with no seam where the design unpacks the record back into separate members only to group it again elsewhere.
rubrics.rationale: The write path spans two packages with an internal interface; converting between grouped and ungrouped forms at the boundary keeps the recurring member triple alive in the very middle of the flow the task asks to clean up.

rubrics.criterion: The patch leaves superseded statistic-carrying leftovers in place: an ungrouped parameter, field, per-column collection, local variable, or return component from the previous design that is now unused, merely forwarded, or duplicated by the new grouping.
rubrics.rationale: The injected design threads the three members as separate carriers through five files; a resolution that adds a grouping but never deletes the old member-by-member plumbing leaves both designs coexisting in the write path.

rubrics.criterion: The change adds throwaway material or drive-by edits: backup or scratch files, stray scaffold code, or unrelated churn such as reformatting, renames, and comment-only rewrites outside the statistics flow it was asked to clean up.
rubrics.rationale: This instance asks for one bounded write-path refactor; leftover scaffolding and opportunistic edits are a concrete failure mode of refactoring tasks on this repository, and the diff to the checked-out base should stay within the requested flow.

rubrics.criterion: Written parquet files carry exactly the same statistics as before at every level: identical page-header Statistics for both header sizes, identical chunk metadata maxima, minima, and null-count totals, and identical per-page ColumnIndex null counts.
rubrics.rationale: The record being regrouped is exactly what ends up serialized in three separate file-format structures; the unit-test suite asserting column-index null-count behavior and read-back of written files is the safety net for this specific case.

rubrics.criterion: The refactor breaks the omit-statistics contract somewhere: a column tagged to omit statistics starts emitting min, max, or null-count values, or a column that must report null counts loses them.
rubrics.rationale: The omit-statistics branch is the sharpest behavioral edge in this flow, and regrouping implementations commonly preserve the happy path while dropping the branch that leaves members intentionally empty.

rubrics.criterion: The patch alters page or row-group production outside the statistics flow: different page splits, sizes, encodings, ordering, offsets, or row-group assembly, or statistics bytes that now appear on dictionary pages.
rubrics.rationale: The statistics record is the only thing the request touches, and this repository's tests pin written-file behavior; silent divergence in the unrelated parts of page production is the plausible damage mode of reworking the writer's flush bookkeeping.
